heuristics.statement: The iteration function f(x) = SHA256-r39(x), where a 256-bit value x is interpreted as a 32-byte message, exhibits random-function-like collision and cycle structure: among N total evaluations from W independent starting points, the probability of an internal collision is well-approximated by 1 - exp(-N^2/(2*2^256)), and individual walks of length 2^115 are overwhelmingly likely to remain acyclic.
heuristics.scope: Applied to SHA-256-r39 (39 compression rounds, indices 0-38) with the standard FIPS 180-4 fixed IV, padding, message schedule, and feed-forward. The iteration operates on one-block 32-byte messages, mapping 256-bit digests back to 32-byte inputs.
heuristics.extrapolation: Extrapolated from: (1) the birthday-bound analysis for ideal random functions (Flajolet and Odlyzko, 1990); (2) universal application in the cryptographic literature for all Merkle-Damgard hash functions; (3) empirical validation in every practical birthday-style collision attack (MD5 by Wang et al. 2004, SHA-1 by Stevens et al. 2017, SHA-1 chosen-prefix by Leurent and Peyrin 2020), where achieved rates match the birthday prediction; (4) the van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point method (1999) as standard collision search tool. The 39-round scope retains substantial mixing from the SHA-256 compression function and message schedule.
heuristics.limitations: Not a formal theorem for SHA-256-r39. The heuristic is empirical and design-motivated. SHA-256-r39 has known differential structure permitting sub-birthday attacks (accepted at time_log2 ~ 94), but this does not impede the birthday attack. Iterated walk correlation (each output becomes the next input) is assumed not to change the collision probability; this is established for random functions but unproven for SHA-256-r39.
